question.prompt: In \(\triangle PAT,\) \(\angle P = 36^\circ,\) \(\angle A = 56^\circ,\) and \(PA = 10.\) Points \(U\) and \(G\) lie on sides \(\overline{TP}\) and \(\overline{TA},\) respectively, so that \(PU = AG = 1.\) Let \(M\) and \(N\) be the midpoints of segments \(\overline{PA}\) and \(\overline{UG},\) respectively. What is the degree measure of the acute angle formed by lines \(MN\) and \(PA?\)

solutions.title: Complete a parallelogram
solutions.explanation:
The two midpoints suggest completing a parallelogram so that a triangle midsegment becomes available.

Extend \(PN\) beyond \(N\) to a point \(Q\) with \(NQ=PN\), and join \(Q\) to \(G\) and \(A\). Now \(N\) is the midpoint of both \(PQ\) and \(UG\). These are the diagonals of quadrilateral \(UPGQ\), so that quadrilateral is a parallelogram. Consequently,
\[
GQ\parallel PU\parallel PT,\qquad GQ=PU=AG=1.
\]
In the original triangle,
\[
\angle PTA=180^\circ-36^\circ-56^\circ=88^\circ.
\]
Ray \(GQ\) points in the same direction as ray \(PT\), while ray \(GA\) points opposite to ray \(AT\). Therefore
\[
\angle QGA=180^\circ-88^\circ=92^\circ.
\]
Since \(GQ=AG\), triangle \(QGA\) is isosceles, giving
\[
\angle QAG=\frac{180^\circ-92^\circ}{2}=44^\circ.
\]
The direction of \(GQ\), from \(P\) toward \(T\), places \(Q\) on the opposite side of line \(AG\) from \(P\). Thus ray \(AG\) lies between rays \(AP\) and \(AQ\), and
\[
\angle QAP=\angle QAG+\angle GAP=44^\circ+56^\circ=100^\circ.
\]
Finally, in triangle \(PQA\), points \(M\) and \(N\) are the midpoints of \(PA\) and \(PQ\). The midsegment theorem gives \(MN\parallel AQ\). Hence the acute angle between \(MN\) and \(PA\) is
\[
180^\circ-100^\circ=\boxed{80^\circ}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
